newsitem.title: USA: AMR municipal debt in billions - rating agencies.
newsitem.headline: AMR municipal debt in billions - rating agencies.

text.p: Billions of dollars of AMR Corp's municipal debt could be affected by a pilots strike against American Airlines, according to bond rating agencies.
Standard & Poor's Corp said the airline has $2.8 billion of special facility revenue bonds outstanding. Those bonds, which were issued for airport projects, are rated BB-plus.
Meanwhile, Moody's Investors Service Inc said it rates about $3.14 billion of the airline's variable-rate demand bonds and industrial revenue bonds. Those bonds carry various rating grades.
Rating analysts from Moody's and S&P said if the threatened strike occurs, ratings on American's municipal debt could be placed on review for a possible downgrade.
The analysts also pointed out a strike could be long and costly for the airline.
Industry analysts have said a strike could cost the airline $30 million a day.
